title: Admin activity tamper-detection beacon & handoff automation
creator: Marcus Li
body:
Summary:
We need a resilient, region-aware mechanism to collect admin action events (role changes, privileged API calls, config modifications), produce immutable attestations for each event stream, and automate handing off bundled attestations and raw events to long-term write-once storage for compliance audits. The goal is to provide tamper-detection signals and an automated export path without adding noticeable latency to the control plane.

Motivation and goals:
- Cover admin activity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments, honoring data residency rules per customer region.
- Produce cryptographically-signed event beacons (lightweight attestations) for every event batch to detect tampering between collection and archived storage.
- Ensure archived objects are written to a write-once-backed store (S3 Object Lock / cloud WORM-equivalent) or customer-managed on-prem destination.
- Automate periodic bundling, compression, and offsite handoff with verification receipts and reporting hooks for Console.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not rework existing app-level audit schema. We'll adapt ingestion to current event shape.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Event capture: existing admin action stream (kafka topic admin-events) will be read by a new consumer group 'beacon-writer'. This service must attach region and residency metadata and forward to two parallel paths: (A) low-latency operational copy for Console and (B) buffered bundle queue for attestation/handoff.
2) Beacon generation: the bundler produces a SHA-256 merkle root over each bundle (time-windowed e.g., 5m or 10k events whichever first), signs the root with a short-lived service key (KMS) yielding a JSON attestation blob {bundle_id, root, signer, ts, residency}. Attestations are small and will be persisted inline with the bundle manifest.
3) Write-once handoff: bundle + attestation is uploaded to a configured sink. For Redwood-hosted customers we'll use S3 with Object Lock enabled + retention manifests. For Dedicated/Private we support HTTPS PUSH to customer-managed WORM endpoint or an on-prem connector that performs local immutability primitives.
4) Verification receipt: after upload, the sink returns a storage receipt (etag / object-id / retention id). We store the receipt in a tamper-resistant metadata table and emit Console metrics and an events export audit record.
5) Console integration: Dashboard shows latest bundle watermark per region, upload receipts, and attestation verification status. Automated alerting when receipts fail for >1 bundle or bundle verification mismatch.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full blockchain anchoring vs lightweight signed beacons: chosen lightweight beacons to reduce operational cost and latency; we keep a later-stage ticket to anchor periodic summaries to public timestamping if requested.
- Synchronous signing overhead: signing uses KMS and runs off the hot path; operational copy remains unaffected.
- Bundle size vs searchability: bundles are optimized for archival and legal export, not fast query; Console will continue to read the operational copy for real-time search.

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Week 1: Read-only PoC of bundler service writing attestations to internal dev S3. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/beacon/PR-112)
- Week 2: Integrate KMS signing and add region metadata, unit tests for signature verification (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/beacon/PR-119).
- Week 3: Implement upload adapters: S3-ObjectLock adapter and HTTPS PUSH adapter. E2E test against test buckets with Object Lock.
- Week 4: Console hooks and metrics, alerting rules, and export verification UI.
- Week 5: Canary rollout to internal org, then to a pilot customer with residency constraints.

QA and verification:
- Property tests to ensure identical bundle input -> deterministic merkle root.
- Automated verification that signed attestation verifies against stored bundle after upload.
- Simulated tamper tests: modify a bundle in test sink and ensure verification fails and alert fires.
- Integration tests for residency enforcement: bundles created in region X must be uploaded to sinks tagged X and not cross-region.

Migration and rollouts:
- This will run as a new consumer in parallel to current admin-events consumers. No migration of existing audit schema required. We'll run both in tandem for 2 weeks and compare counts.

Operational runbooks and SRE playbacks:
- runbooks/beacon-upload-failure.md (linked in PR)
- On failed upload, automatic retry with exponential backoff and escalation to oncall if >3 consecutive bundles fail.

Security and compliance notes:
- KMS keys used for signing are rotated quarterly; signing key material never leaves KMS.
- For Dedicated/Private, customers can bring their own KMS; signing plugin will accept customer KMS ARN.
- Data residency enforced via metadata and sink selection; ops must not re-route bundles to other regions.

Open questions and decisions needed:
- Retention vs legal hold API: we need Product to finalize retention windows per customer tier and legal-hold behavior. (PM input requested)
- Do we include per-event secondary hashes to speed partial verification? (tradeoff: larger attestations).

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Admin+Beacon+Design
- PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/beacon/pull/112
- Signing integration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/beacon/pull/119
- Dashboard mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleMockups

Recent activity (timeline):
- 2025-01-10 CREATED by Marcus Li: initial scope and design sketch.
- 2025-01-16 COMMENT by Asha Patel: added region tagging requirement and suggested 5m bundle window default.
- 2025-01-22 UPDATE by Marcus Li: PoC consumer and bundler PoC merged to dev; basic attestation format verified.
- 2025-01-29 REVIEW by Security (Samantha Reyes): requested KMS usage patterns and explicit ROT13 for key IDs in logs. Security approved subject to KMS key policy changes.
- 2025-02-02 UPDATE by Asha Patel: KMS integration PR opened (PR-119), S3 adapter completed for dev bucket, creating canary checklist.

Acceptance criteria:
- Bundler service produces signed attestations for 100% of admin bundles in pilot org.
- Bundles uploaded to write-once sink and receipts persisted within 24 hours for >99.9% of bundles.
- Console displays bundle watermarks and upload receipts; alerts fire on verification failures.
- Security review completed and key rotation documented.

Follow-ups (future tickets):
- Add public anchoring of weekly summary roots to a public timestamping service.
- Provide fast partial verification index for legal teams (event-level offsets).
- Add automated legal-hold API and cross-tenant export authorization flows.

Notes for reviewers:
- Please evaluate the attestation schema in the design doc and comment on whether additional signing fields are required for cross-tenant verification.
- Security and PM: confirm retention windows and legal-hold semantics before release.
